extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in arts/culture, free speech, and Indian legal controversies
extracted.subtask_short: stand-up comedy legal risks in India
extracted.subtask_description: News article describing legal, procedural, and social risks faced by stand-up comedians in India — arrest for allegedly offending religious sentiments, preemptive detention, political complaints, and platform pressure. Useful for understanding legal constraints on producing and performing comedy in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentionally hurting religious sentiments is a criminal offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-up comedy has become hugely popular in recent years in India, where intentionally hurting religious sentiments is a criminal offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedians risk criminal complaints and arrest if their material is judged to hurt religious sentiments; this legal framework shapes what material is safe to perform and can lead to prosecutions or censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemptive arrest for planned remarks ('going to' make jokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indore police initially claimed Faruqui had not made the jokes during a performance; the city’s superintendent of police said Faruqui had not made the jokes during a performance but was 'going to'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities may act on allegations about planned or intended remarks, leading to arrest before any allegedly objectionable content is actually delivered; performers can therefore be detained based on intent or anticipated speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vagueness of allegations affects bail decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Supreme Court bench said the allegations against Faruqui were vague and granted him interim bail after three lower courts refused to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may consider the specificity and clarity of allegations when deciding bail; vague or poorly substantiated claims can support grant of interim bail, while lower courts may respond differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement (or lack) of investigation/evidence before arrest
rubrics_metrics.description: In his plea, Faruqui said police did not conduct investigations or collect any evidence before arresting him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural norms such as conducting investigations and collecting evidence prior to arrest are relevant to legal challenges; failure to investigate can be cited in pleas and appeals as improper enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political complaints can trigger legal action
rubrics_metrics.description: The comedian was arrested following a complaint by the son of a politician from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints lodged by politically connected individuals or party affiliates can prompt police action and escalate legal risk for performers, suggesting political influence is an important contextual factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure from nationalist groups affects creators and platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The ire of Hindu nationalist groups aligned with Modi’s party has also caught streaming platforms off guard. Many of their shows have faced boycott calls and legal cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond direct criminal charges, creators and distribution platforms face boycotts, legal complaints, and other pressures from political or nationalist groups; this can lead to content removal, self-censorship, or legal disputes.
